cases.title: Bastion security group opened to 0.0.0.0/0 on SSH
cases.why: The most common real incident. Someone is locked out, widens the rule to unblock themselves, and the temporary fix is never reverted.

cases.title: New security group allowing every protocol on every port from anywhere
cases.why: Written during an outage to rule out the network as a cause, then left in place because the outage had a different root cause and nobody revisited it.

cases.title: PostgreSQL exposed to the internet through aws_vpc_security_group_ingress_rule
cases.why: The newer singular rule resource uses different attribute names (cidr_ipv4, ip_protocol). Scanners written against the inline block shape read it as having no rules at all and report nothing.

cases.title: MySQL source range widened from a /24 to a /8
cases.why: The diff shows one string changing and still contains a CIDR, so it reads as scoped. It admits sixteen million more addresses than it did.

cases.title: S3 block_public_policy turned off
cases.why: Disabling the guard exposes nothing by itself, which is exactly why it gets approved. The bucket policy that makes it matter arrives in a later change.

cases.title: Production database given a public endpoint
cases.why: Usually done to let a BI tool or a contractor connect without setting up peering. The security group becomes the only remaining control.

cases.title: Internal load balancer flipped to internet-facing
cases.why: A one-character diff, false to true, that changes the reachability of every target behind the load balancer, including targets added later by other teams.

cases.title: Network ACL entry allowing 0.0.0.0/0 into a private subnet
cases.why: The network ACL is the subnet's independent boundary and the only control still standing when a security group is wrong. An allow-all entry removes the second layer while the first still looks correct.

cases.title: Unrestricted egress added to a workload security group
cases.why: Copied from the provider documentation's example block, which uses 0.0.0.0/0 on protocol -1. It is the path data leaves by.

cases.title: EKS control plane endpoint made public with no allow-list
cases.why: Enabled to make kubectl work from a laptop. The Kubernetes API is then internet-reachable with IAM as the only barrier.

cases.title: Subnet switched to auto-assign public IPs
cases.why: Changes the character of every instance launched into the subnet from then on, including instances created by autoscaling long after this review.

cases.title: Security group whose rules are computed at apply time
cases.why: The rules come from a module output that Terraform cannot resolve during plan. A reviewer sees an empty ingress list and approves it. The tool has to say it cannot review this rather than say it found nothing.

cases.title: Application port 8080 opened directly to the internet
cases.why: Added to debug a load balancer health check. It routes around the load balancer, and with it TLS termination, the WAF and the access logs. The port is not a database port, so a rule that only knows about well-known services says nothing at all.

cases.title: Production database destroyed because its block was deleted
cases.why: A module refactor removes a resource block. Terraform renders one line with a minus sign, and the data is not in version control.

cases.title: Database replaced because an immutable attribute changed
cases.why: Changing the subnet group forces recreation. Terraform shows -/+ and the reviewer reads it as an update. The new instance comes up empty.

cases.title: NAT gateway replaced destroy-first, cutting egress for the subnet
cases.why: Without create_before_destroy there is a window with no NAT gateway. Every instance in the private subnet loses outbound connectivity for the duration.

cases.title: Deletion protection disabled and final snapshot skipped in one change
cases.why: Neither attribute changes anything on apply. Together they remove both controls that would have stopped, or made recoverable, the next destroy.

cases.title: Plan computed against a state that no longer matches reality
cases.why: Someone changed the security group in the console. Every diff in this plan is a diff against a picture that is already wrong, and applying it silently reverts their change.

cases.title: Sensitive value changes with the diff redacted
cases.why: Terraform prints (sensitive value) on both sides. The change is real, unreviewable from the plan, and anything still holding the old value breaks at apply.

cases.title: A security group change that also rewrites an IAM role
cases.why: The pull request says it adjusts a security group. The plan also modifies an IAM role, which is the kind of thing that gets approved by association with the change that was actually reviewed.

cases.title: Bucket policy that Terraform cannot resolve before apply
cases.why: The policy is rendered from a data source that resolves at apply time. Approving the plan approves a policy document nobody has read.

cases.title: KMS key destroyed while data encrypted under it remains
cases.why: Deleting the key is a single line. Everything encrypted with it becomes permanently unreadable, including backups taken before the change.

cases.title: CloudWatch log group replaced, discarding retained events
cases.why: Renaming a log group replaces it. The retained events go with the old one, which matters most in exactly the situation you need them for.

cases.title: A public web server serving 443 to the internet
cases.why: This is what a correct public service looks like. A tool that calls this critical is a tool people turn off.

cases.title: A tag change on a security group that was already open to the world
cases.why: The single most important negative control. The exposure is real but it is not this change's doing. A tool that blocks this pull request is blocking the wrong pull request, and teaches the team that its findings are noise.

cases.title: An SSH rule narrowed from the internet to the VPN range
cases.why: A strict improvement. Reporting it would mean the tool cannot tell the direction of a change, only that one happened.

cases.title: A launch template replaced, which loses nothing
cases.why: Replacement is only alarming when something irreplaceable goes with it. Treating every -/+ as critical is how a tool becomes background noise.
